subject: Biology
title: Endocrine Glands, Signalling, & Chemical Taxonomy
learningObjectives: Define hormones as non-nutrient intercellular chemical messengers produced in trace quantities
Classify hormones into 4 chemical categories: Peptides/Proteins, Steroids, Iodothyronines, and Amino Acid Derivatives
Predict hormone receptor location based on lipid vs. water solubility
content:
Hormones are non-nutrient, intercellular chemical messengers produced in trace quantities by ductless Endocrine Glands and secreted directly into systemic circulation to regulate distant target organ physiology.

```
                           CHEMICAL CLASSES OF HORMONES
                                         │
     ┌──────────────────┬────────────────┴────────────────┬──────────────────┐
     ▼                  ▼                                 ▼                  ▼
PEPTIDE / PROTEIN    STEROID HORMONES                IODOTHYRONINES      AMINO ACID DERIVATIVES
├── Insulin, Glucagon├── Derived from Cholesterol     ├── T₃ (Triiodo)    ├── Epinephrine (Tyrosine)
├── Pituitary/Hypo. ├── Cortisol, Aldosterone         └── T₄ (Thyroxine)  ├── Norepinephrine (Tyrosine)
└── PTH, Calcitonin  └── Testosterone, Estrogens                           └── Melatonin (Tryptophan)
```

### 1.1 Chemical Taxonomy Matrix

| Chemical Category | Biochemical Precursor | Key Representative Hormones | Solubility & Receptor Location |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Peptides & Polypeptides** | Amino acid polymers | Insulin, Glucagon, Pituitary Hormones (GH, TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH, Oxytocin, ADH), PTH, Calcitonin, Thymosins, ANF, Secretin, CCK | Water-soluble; Hydrophilic; **Membrane-Bound Surface Receptors** |
| **Steroid Hormones** | **Cholesterol** (CPPP core) | Cortisol, Aldosterone, Testosterone, Progesterone, Estradiol (Estrogen) | Lipid-soluble; Hydrophobic; **Intracellular / Nuclear Receptors** |
| **Iodothyronines** | Iodinated **Tyrosine** residues | $T_3$ (Triiodothyronine) and $T_4$ (Tetraiodothyronine / Thyroxine) | Lipid-soluble; Hydrophobic; **Nuclear Receptors** |
| **Amino Acid Derivatives** | Single Amino Acids (**Tyrosine** or **Tryptophan**) | **Catecholamines:** Epinephrine (Adrenaline), Norepinephrine (from Tyrosine); **Melatonin** (from Tryptophan) | Water-soluble; Hydrophilic; **Membrane-Bound Surface Receptors** |

conceptBreakdown.heading: Hydrophilic vs Lipophilic Transport in Blood
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Hydrophilic peptide and catecholamine hormones dissolve freely in plasma water. Lipophilic steroid and thyroid hormones travel in systemic circulation largely bound to plasma carrier proteins (e.g., Albumin, Thyroid-Binding Globulin TBG, Corticosteroid-Binding Globulin CBG).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Steroid Precursor: The CPPP Ring
conceptBreakdown.explanation: All steroid hormones are synthesized from cholesterol via the Cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene (CPPP) four-ring steroid nucleus in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria.
